subject: BrightWays SDK kickstart: env checklist, sample apps, next steps
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@brightways.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + SDK quickstart request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the productive discovery call earlier — spent a few minutes afterwards with our engineering lead and we have a couple of concrete asks to get a small pilot spinning up:

1) A minimal SDK quickstart (Python and TypeScript) we can run locally to validate auth + routing.
2) Sample that shows: structured output for tool-calling, simple embeddings + reranker flow.
3) A short checklist of environment variables, token scopes, and any required firewall/VPC settings.

If you can share a concise package or repo we can clone and test in our dev laptops (macOS + Ubuntu WSL), that would be ideal. Also copy in procurement so they can track any contract items.

Proposed success criteria for our pilot:
- Local end-to-end: produce an embedding for a test document, rerank two responses, and call a mock tool via structured output.
- Keep token costs < $X/day during tests (we'll validate with your team).

Appreciate a short MAP and any attachments.

Thanks,
Alex
Lead Engineer, BrightWays AI

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@brightways.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-21T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + SDK quickstart request

Alex — thanks, great to talk. Below is a compact post-call implementation checklist plus the quickstarts we recommend for a fast local pilot. I attached a small zip with the sample apps and a one-page mutual action plan (MAP-BrightWays.pdf).

TL;DR next steps
- We’ll provision a short-lived developer API key for you to run the sandbox samples (scope: inference.read, inference.embed, inference.rerank).
- You clone rdw-samples and run the Python or TS flow locally.
- We run a 60–90 min hands-on session with your eng team to validate tool-calling and the reranker wiring.

Attachments: rdw-sdk-quickstart.zip (includes /python, /typescript samples, README), MAP-BrightWays.pdf

Environment checklist (local pilot)
- OS: macOS Monterey+ or Ubuntu 20.04+. Node 18+ for TS samples. Python 3.10+.
- Install: pip install redwood-inference (or npm i @redwood-inference/sdk) — packaged wrappers included in zip.
- Env vars:
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY (we will send a short-lived dev key)
  - REDWOOD_API_URL (defaults to https://api.redwood.ai; set to your private endpoint for Private deployments)
  - REDWOOD_REGION (us-east-1)
  - RDW_ROUTING_POLICY (optional) — values: latency|cost|balanced
- Optional local KMS mock: if you validate client-side encryption/decryption, we include a simple KMS shim in /tools/kms-mock.

Auth and scopes
- Dev key will be limited to inference.read, inference.embed, inference.rerank. No admin scopes.
- For Dedicated/Private pilots we'll provide a scoped service account with KMS roles tied to your tenant.

Routing and fallbacks
- The sample uses RDW_ROUTING_POLICY=balanced by default; code demonstrates explicit route pinning to a model variant (e.g., redwood/gpt-instruct-2-1q).
- We include a local override file (rdw.config.json) so you can force a cheaper quantized variant for throughput experiments.

Structured output & tool calling example (Python snippet from /python/tool_call.py)
- The sample shows a schema-based tool call: the model returns {"tool_call": {"name":"lookup_price","args": {"sku":"BWAY-42"}}} and the sample harness invokes a mock HTTP tool and injects the result back to the model for a follow-up completion.

Embeddings + reranker flow
- /python/embeddings_demo.py: creates embeddings for 10 sample docs (local JSONL), stores vectors in an in-memory FAISS index (we ship a minimal wrapper), performs an approximate nearest neighbor search, then sends top-5 candidates to the reranker endpoint to produce final ordering.

Local test commands (examples included in README)
- python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
- pip install -r python/requirements.txt
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key> REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai python python/embeddings_demo.py

- For TS: cd typescript && npm ci && REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key> node dist/embeddings_demo.js

Success criteria (proposal)
- Unit smoke: both python and ts samples run end-to-end locally within 30 minutes.
- Feature check: tool-call returned structured payload and mock tool invoked; reranker changes ordering vs. baseline.

Proposed dates:
- We can send a dev key by EOD tomorrow and book the hands-on session Wed/Thu next week. Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate calendars.

If this aligns I’ll share the dev key + GitHub link to the samples repo.

— Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@brightways.ai>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-22T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + SDK quickstart request

Alex — quick note from success/regional CS side. Happy to run the 60–90 min workshop and align acceptance criteria. Couple of pragmatic items we typically include in the pilot MAP:

- Engineering contact + backstop (who will confirm the pilot success).
- Data handling checklist (are test documents PII-free? => we recommend sanitized data for the first run).
- Day-of checklist: stable wifi, local ports 8000/9000 available (mock tools), allowed outbound to https://api.redwood.ai and to our workshop share link.

I added the HubSpot link here for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890 — I’ll create the workshop invite once Alex confirms preferred slot (Wed/Thu windows).

Karthik — please add a short architecture slide to the repo that shows where reranker runs (client vs. RDW-hosted) and the recommended quantized model for initial throughput.

Thanks,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
